subject: Dedicated pool: queue prioritization & fallback plan (MotorLeaf)
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@motorleaf.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@motorleaf.com
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated pool: request for queue prioritization + fallback runbook

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're finalizing the Dedicated capacity request for our Black Friday style promotion window (Jan 18-22) and have a couple of specific asks around queueing behavior and fallback. Summary below: 

- We need soft guarantees that during peak promotion traffic we get prioritized inflight concurrency for the SKUs we reserve (we expect bursts up to 6x baseline).
- If the pool hits pressure, we'd like a documented fallback that: 1) routes lower-priority / background jobs to a pre-agreed sandbox; 2) gracefully degrades generation length before impacting latency SLOs; 3) defines crediting if throughput drops below the committed floor.

Attached is a short PDF with our usage profile and sample traces. Can Redwood produce a short runbook + a proposal for how this would appear in the Dedicated addendum? Procurement will need a clear slide or single-pager to include in our approval packet.

Best,
Emily Park
Head of Integrations, MotorLeaf
Attachments: motorleaf_sla_request.pdf, motorleaf_usage_sample.csv
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Emily Park <emily.park@motorleaf.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: request for queue prioritization + fallback runbook

Hi Emily —

Appreciate the detail and the traces, that helps. High level response and next steps: 

1) Prioritization: we can offer "soft priority lanes" inside the Dedicated pool that favor your tenant's inflight KV and concurrency. This isn't hard isolation, but it statistically reduces preemption risk for pinned SKUs. We need to finalize the concurrency band (tokens/slot) tied to your commit.

2) Fallback runbook: happy to draft a short playbook that covers routing background traffic to a sandbox namespace, automatic response-length throttles, and an operator-first escalation flow. We typically also include a token-backed credit schedule for missed throughput thresholds.

3) Deliverables & timing: I'll draft the runbook and an amendment sketch by EOD Wed (Dec 8) and loop in Laura for the contractual language and Ben for capacity planning/observability hooks. Could you confirm the peak windows and whether the burst is regional (US-west) or multi-region? That changes routing options.

I'll attach a working draft of our standard fallback playbook in my follow-up.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_fallback_playbook.md (will send in follow-up)
From: Emily Park <emily.park@motorleaf.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@motorleaf.com
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: request for queue prioritization + fallback runbook

Jonas —

Thanks, that's great. Peak windows are Jan 18 00:00 - Jan 22 23:59 PST; traffic originates primarily from our US-west stack with a smaller tail in US-east. Burst factor is ~6x baseline for generative length 512 tokens; background jobs are lower priority but run concurrently on different routes.

Procurement specifically asked for: a) a single-line crediting formula for missed throughput (we can live with a capped credit per incident), and b) a short operator checklist we can hand to on-call during the promotion.

If you can get the draft by Wed EOD, procurement can include it in the packet for our Dec 14 approval meeting.

--
Emily
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Emily Park <emily.park@motorleaf.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: request for queue prioritization + fallback runbook

Emily —

Attached: proposed_fallback_playbook.md (short runbook), and a one-line crediting table snippet: 

- Crediting: if sustained throughput for reserved SKUs falls below 85% of contracted baseline for > 15 minutes during a confirmed promotion window, Redwood issues a credit equal to 0.5x the per-hour reserved capacity charge for each contiguous 15-minute degradation block, capped at 48 hours per promotion.

- Operator checklist (summary):
  * 00:00 — confirm dedication pools in US-west are healthy via Console > Pools
  * 00:15 — validate route prioritization flags (redwoodctl routes list --priority motorleaf)
  * 00:30 — verify KV cache hit rates above 70% and activate length-throttle policy if tail latency > 500ms
  * Escalation — page Redwood SRE if automated fallback fails to recover in 10 minutes.

Laura: can you review the crediting language and convert into an amendment paragraph suitable for the SOW?
Ben: please confirm capacity carve (nodes and soft-priority margin) that maps to Emily's 6x burst number — we should include pre-warming guidance.

Emily — if that looks reasonable I'll convert to a one-pager for your approval before Dec 14.

Best,
Jonas

Attachments: proposed_fallback_playbook.md
